1. Escalation Tiers
Support operates a three-tier escalation model:

Tier 1 - Frontline Support, handles general troubleshooting and account questions.

Tier 2 - Technical Support, handles complex product issues and API troubleshooting.

Tier 3 - Engineering On-Call, handles suspected bugs, data issues, and outages.
2. When to Escalate
Tickets should be escalated to Tier 2 if unresolved after 2 hours for P1, 8 hours for P2, or 3
business days for P3. Any ticket involving suspected data loss or security concerns must be
escalated to Tier 3 and the Security team immediately, regardless of priority.
3. Escalation Process
Escalations are submitted via the 'Escalate' button in Zendesk, which automatically pages
the relevant on-call Tier 2 or Tier 3 responder through PagerDuty and creates a linked
incident thread in Slack.
4. Executive Escalation

AcmeTech Solutions Inc. — Customer_Support — Internal & Confidential
Page 4
Strategic or at-risk Enterprise accounts may be escalated to the VP of Customer Support
for executive-level attention. Executive escalations are logged in the Customer Success
platform (Gainsight) and reviewed weekly in the Customer Health meeting.
5. Roles and Responsibilities
Key roles in the escalation process:

Tier 1 Agent - initial triage and escalation trigger.

Tier 2 Responder - resolves complex technical issues, escalates to Tier 3 if a product
bug is confirmed.

Tier 3 On-Call Engineer - investigates suspected bugs, data issues, or outages.

VP of Customer Support - handles executive escalations for strategic accounts.
6. Escalation Handoff Requirements
Every escalation must include a completed handoff summary (issue description,
reproduction steps, customer impact, and prior troubleshooting attempted) before being
accepted by the next tier, to avoid redundant customer questioning.
7. Cross-Team Escalations
Issues requiring input from Engineering, Product, or Legal beyond standard Tier 3
involvement are routed through a Cross-Functional Escalation request in Jira, reviewed
daily by a rotating triage owner from each relevant team.

AcmeTech Solutions Inc. — Customer_Support — Internal & Confidential
Page 5
8. Escalation Metrics and Reporting
Support leadership reviews monthly escalation volume and time-to-resolution metrics by
tier, using outliers to identify recurring product issues warranting a permanent fix rather
than repeated manual escalation.
9. Preventing Escalation Fatigue
Tier 2 and Tier 3 responders are limited to a maximum on-call escalation load per week,
tracked via PagerDuty, with load-balancing across the broader technical support pool if any
individual approaches the limit.
10. Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can a customer request escalation directly, bypassing Tier 1?

A: Enterprise customers can request escalation directly through their dedicated Slack
channel, which is monitored by Tier 2 responders.

Q: What if Tier 2 and Tier 3 disagree on whether something is a bug?

A: The Tier 3 on-call engineer has final technical determination, escalated to the
Engineering Manager if unresolved.

Q: Are escalations tracked separately from standard ticket metrics?

A: Yes, escalations have a dedicated Zendesk tag and appear in a separate escalation
dashboard reviewed weekly.

13. Glossary of Terms
Key terms used throughout this guide:

Tier 1/2/3 - the three-tier escalation structure from frontline support to engineering
on-call.

Handoff Summary - the required documentation accompanying every escalation between
tiers.

Cross-Functional Escalation - an escalation requiring input from Engineering, Product, or
Legal.

Gainsight - the platform used to track executive-level account escalations.
14. Appendix: Escalation Path Example
An Enterprise customer reports intermittent data sync failures between AcmeSync and their
Salesforce instance. Tier 1 confirms it's not a known configuration issue and escalates to

Tier 2 within the 2-hour P1 window. Tier 2 investigation reveals a likely bug in the sync retry
logic, warranting escalation to Tier 3 Engineering On-Call, who confirms the bug and ships
a hotfix outside the standard release train given the P1 severity and confirmed product
defect.
15. Continuous Improvement
The Escalation Guide is reviewed quarterly against actual escalation data to identify
whether thresholds (e.g., the 2-hour P1 Tier 2 trigger) remain appropriate as ticket volume
and product complexity evolve. Recommendations for threshold changes are proposed by
the VP of Customer Support and approved jointly with Engineering leadership, since tighter
thresholds increase on-call load on Tier 3 responders.
16. Training for New Escalation Responders
New Tier 2 and Tier 3 responders shadow at least 5 live escalations before joining the
on-call rotation independently, and complete a certification checklist covering the handoff
summary format, PagerDuty tooling, and the Cross-Functional Escalation process before
being added to the rotation schedule.

but lacks billing system access to correct it, so the ticket is escalated directly to the Billing

hours.

1. Platform Uptime SLA
AcmeTech guarantees 99.9% monthly uptime for Enterprise tier customers and 99.5% for
Growth tier customers, measured against core API and application availability. Starter tier
does not include a formal uptime guarantee.
2. Support Response Time SLA
Response time targets by tier and priority:

Enterprise: P1 - 1 hour, P2 - 4 hours, P3 - 1 business day, P4 - 2 business days.

Growth: P1 - 4 hours, P2 - 8 hours, P3 - 2 business days, P4 - 4 business days.

Starter: P1 - 8 hours, P2 - 1 business day, P3 - 3 business days, P4 - 5 business days.
3. Resolution Time Targets
While resolution time varies by issue complexity, AcmeTech targets resolving 90% of P1
issues within 4 hours and 90% of P2 issues within 1 business day for Enterprise customers.
4. Service Credits
If monthly uptime falls below the guaranteed threshold, Enterprise customers are eligible for
service credits ranging from 5% to 30% of their monthly subscription fee, applied

automatically to the following month's invoice, as detailed in the customer's Master Service
Agreement.
5. SLA Exclusions
The uptime SLA does not apply to downtime resulting from:

Scheduled maintenance windows communicated at least 48 hours in advance.

Force majeure events beyond AcmeTech's reasonable control.

Customer-caused issues, including misconfiguration or exceeding documented rate
limits.

Third-party service outages outside AcmeTech's direct infrastructure (e.g., a customer's
own Salesforce instance being down).
6. Measurement Methodology
Uptime is measured via automated synthetic monitoring checks against core API and
application endpoints at 1-minute intervals from multiple geographic locations, with monthly
uptime percentage calculated as (total minutes - downtime minutes) / total minutes.
7. Requesting a Service Credit
Customers must submit a service credit request within 30 days of the month in which the
SLA was not met, including supporting evidence if available; AcmeTech independently
verifies against internal monitoring data before issuing credit.

Standard support hours are 8 AM-8 PM in the customer's regional business hours for
Growth and Starter tiers; Enterprise customers receive 24/7 coverage for P1 and P2 issues
as described in the Support SOP.
9. Planned Maintenance Notifications
Planned maintenance likely to affect availability is announced via the status page and email
to account administrators at least 48 hours in advance, scheduled during low-traffic
windows determined by historical usage patterns per region.

This SLA document is reviewed annually and may be updated with 60 days' notice to
existing customers; existing contractual SLA commitments in a signed Master Service

1. Ticket Intake
Customer tickets are received through three channels: in-app chat, email
(support@acmetech.com), and the Enterprise dedicated Slack channel. All tickets are
automatically logged in Zendesk and assigned a priority level.
2. Priority Levels
Tickets are triaged into four priority levels:

P1 (Urgent) - platform outage or complete inability to use core functionality.

P2 (High) - major feature broken with no workaround.

P3 (Medium) - feature issue with an available workaround.

P4 (Low) - general question, minor bug, or feature request.
3. Ticket Handling Process
Support agents must acknowledge every new ticket within the applicable SLA window (see
SLA document), gather reproduction details, and either resolve the ticket directly or
escalate to Tier 2 Support or Engineering following the Escalation Guide.
4. Tools

Support agents use Zendesk for ticket management, Intercom for in-app chat, and a shared
Notion knowledge base for internal troubleshooting runbooks. Screen-share sessions with

All customer-facing communication must be professional, empathetic, and jargon-free.
Agents should provide a status update at least once every 24 hours on any open P1 or P2
ticket, even if no resolution has been reached.
6. Agent Onboarding and Certification
New support agents complete a 3-week certification program covering product training,
tooling (Zendesk, Intercom), and shadowing before handling tickets independently. Agents
must pass a certification assessment with a score of 85% or higher before graduating to
independent ticket ownership.
7. Quality Assurance
A random sample of 5% of resolved tickets per agent per month is reviewed by a QA Lead
against a standardized rubric covering accuracy, tone, and adherence to SOP. Scores
below 80% trigger a coaching conversation with the agent's team lead.

90% or higher across all tiers, reviewed weekly by Support leadership with team-level
breakdowns.

Support agents are expected to flag outdated or missing knowledge base articles as they're
encountered; the Knowledge Management team reviews and updates flagged articles
within 5 business days.
10. Handling Difficult Conversations
Agents are trained to de-escalate frustrated customers using AcmeTech's 'Acknowledge,
Apologize, Act' framework, and may transfer a conversation to a team lead if a customer
becomes abusive, without requiring further justification.

Enterprise customers have access to 24/7 support coverage for P1 issues through a
follow-the-sun model across the Austin, Dublin, and Bengaluru support hubs. Growth and
Starter tier support operates standard business hours (8 AM-8 PM local time) Monday

1. Overview
The AcmeTech REST API allows customers and partners to programmatically manage
workflows, integrations, and user data. The base URL for all API v3 requests is
https://api.acmetech.com/v3/.
2. Authentication
The API uses OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow for server-to-server integrations. Access
tokens are valid for 60 minutes and must be included in the Authorization header as a
Bearer token.
API keys for testing can be generated in the Developer Console under Settings > API
Access. Production API keys require admin approval within the customer's account.
3. Rate Limits
Standard tier accounts are limited to 100 requests per minute per API key. Enterprise tier
accounts are limited to 1,000 requests per minute. Requests exceeding the limit receive an
HTTP 429 response with a Retry-After header.
4. Core Endpoints
Commonly used endpoints:

AcmeTech Solutions Inc. — Engineering — Internal & Confidential
Page 4

GET /workflows - list all workflows for the authenticated account.

POST /workflows - create a new workflow.

POST /workflows/{id}/execute - trigger a manual workflow run.

GET /integrations - list connected third-party integrations.

GET /audit-logs - retrieve audit log entries (Enterprise tier only).
5. Webhooks
Customers can subscribe to real-time events (workflow.completed, workflow.failed,
integration.disconnected) via webhooks configured in the Developer Console. Webhook
payloads are signed using HMAC-SHA256, and the signature is included in the
X-AcmeTech-Signature header.
6. Error Handling
The API returns standard HTTP status codes. Error responses include a JSON body with
an 'error_code' and 'message' field. Common error codes include INVALID_REQUEST
(400), UNAUTHORIZED (401), RATE_LIMITED (429), and INTERNAL_ERROR (500).
7. SDKs
Official SDKs are maintained for Python, Node.js, and Java, available via PyPI, npm, and
Maven Central respectively. Community-maintained SDKs for Go and Ruby are listed in the
developer portal but are not officially supported.

AcmeTech Solutions Inc. — Engineering — Internal & Confidential
Page 5
8. Pagination
List endpoints support cursor-based pagination via the 'limit' (default 25, max 100) and
'cursor' query parameters. Responses include a 'next_cursor' field in the pagination
metadata block; a null value indicates the last page has been reached.
9. Filtering and Sorting
Most list endpoints support filtering via query parameters matching the resource's field
names (e.g., 'GET /workflows?status=active') and sorting via a 'sort' parameter prefixed
with '-' for descending order (e.g., 'sort=-created_at').
10. Idempotency
POST requests that create resources support an 'Idempotency-Key' header; sending the
same key within a 24-hour window returns the original response rather than creating a
duplicate resource, useful for safely retrying failed requests.
11. Sandbox Environment
Developers can test integrations against a sandbox environment at
https://sandbox-api.acmetech.com/v3/, which mirrors production behavior but resets all
data every 24 hours and does not send real notifications or process real payments.
12. Versioning and Deprecation Policy

AcmeTech Solutions Inc. — Engineering — Internal & Confidential
Page 6
AcmeTech supports each major API version for a minimum of 18 months after a successor
version's release. Deprecation notices are sent to all registered developers at least 12
months before a version is fully retired, with deprecation warnings also surfaced via the
'Sunset' HTTP response header.
13. Example Request

Example: creating a workflow via cURL.

curl -X POST https://api.acmetech.com/v3/workflows -H 'Authorization: Bearer {token}' -H
'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name": "New Lead Notification", "trigger":
"salesforce.lead.created"}'

A successful response returns HTTP 201 with the created workflow object, including its
generated 'id' and 'created_at' timestamp.
14. Common Integration Patterns
Most customers combine webhooks for real-time event notification with periodic polling of
the '/workflows/{id}/runs' endpoint as a reconciliation safety net, ensuring no execution is
missed even if a webhook delivery fails.
15. Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What happens if my webhook endpoint is down?

A: AcmeTech retries webhook delivery up to 5 times with exponential backoff over 24
hours before marking the delivery as failed and surfacing it in the Developer Console.

1. High-Level Overview
AcmeTech's platform is built as a microservices architecture comprising approximately 45
independently deployed services. All external traffic enters through the API Gateway, which
handles authentication, rate limiting, and request routing.
2. Core Services
Key services include:

Auth Service - handles authentication (OAuth2, SAML SSO) and issues JWT access
tokens.

Workflow Engine - the core automation engine that executes customer-defined
workflows.

Integration Hub - manages connections to 200+ third-party SaaS applications.

Notification Service - handles email, SMS, and in-app notification delivery.

Billing Service - integrates with Stripe for subscription billing and usage-based metering.
3. Data Layer
Each service owns its own PostgreSQL database following a database-per-service pattern.
Cross-service data access happens exclusively through service APIs or asynchronous
events published to Kafka, never through direct database access.

AcmeTech Solutions Inc. — Engineering — Internal & Confidential
Page 4
Analytical workloads are served from a separate Snowflake data warehouse, populated via
nightly ETL jobs orchestrated by Airflow.
4. Event-Driven Architecture
Services communicate asynchronously via Kafka topics for non-blocking operations such
as workflow execution logs, audit events, and notification triggers. Each service publishes
domain events following the CloudEvents specification.
5. Infrastructure and Deployment
All services run as containerized workloads on Amazon EKS across three environments:
dev, staging, and production. Production spans three AWS regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1,
ap-southeast-1) for latency and redundancy purposes.
Infrastructure is defined as code using Terraform, with all changes reviewed via pull request
and applied through a GitOps pipeline (ArgoCD).
6. Observability
The platform uses Datadog for metrics and dashboards, OpenTelemetry for distributed
tracing, and centralized logging via the ELK stack. Service-level objectives (SLOs) target
99.9% uptime for core API endpoints.
7. Service Ownership Model

AcmeTech Solutions Inc. — Engineering — Internal & Confidential
Page 5
Every service has a single owning squad recorded in the internal Service Catalog, which
also tracks the service's tier (Tier 1 customer-facing, Tier 2 internal-critical, Tier 3
internal-supporting), on-call rotation, and current SLO attainment.
8. API Gateway Details
The API Gateway (built on Kong) handles TLS termination, authentication token validation,
request routing based on path-based rules, and enforces per-client rate limiting before
requests reach downstream services. Gateway configuration changes go through the same
pull-request review process as application code.
9. Caching Strategy
Read-heavy services use a two-tier caching strategy: an in-process LRU cache for hot data
(sub-millisecond access) backed by a shared Redis cluster (single-digit millisecond access)
for cross-instance consistency. Cache invalidation is handled via Kafka events published
on write.
10. Data Warehouse and Analytics
The Snowflake data warehouse ingests data from all 45 services via nightly
Airflow-orchestrated ETL jobs, plus select high-value streams ingested in near-real-time via
Kafka Connect. The warehouse powers the internal Analytics Dashboard and the
customer-facing Insights feature in AcmeFlow.
11. Multi-Tenancy Model

AcmeTech Solutions Inc. — Engineering — Internal & Confidential
Page 6
AcmeTech uses a shared-database, tenant-isolated-by-row model for most services, with
row-level security enforced at the PostgreSQL level via tenant_id scoping on every table.
Enterprise customers requiring physical data isolation can be provisioned into a dedicated
single-tenant deployment as a paid add-on.
12. Scalability and Capacity Planning
Core services are provisioned with auto-scaling policies targeting 60% average CPU
utilization, with capacity reviewed quarterly by the Platform team ahead of known seasonal
peaks (e.g., end-of-quarter customer usage spikes).
13. Third-Party Dependencies
Beyond AWS, the platform depends on Stripe (billing), Okta (SSO), Twilio (SMS
notifications), SendGrid (transactional email), and Snowflake (analytics). Each third-party
dependency has a documented fallback or degraded-mode behavior in the Service
Catalog.
14. Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How are cross-service transactions handled without distributed transactions?

A: AcmeTech uses the Saga pattern with compensating actions published as Kafka
events, avoiding distributed two-phase commit.

Q: What happens if Kafka is unavailable?

A: Services buffer events locally for up to 5 minutes and degrade gracefully by falling
back to synchronous API calls for critical paths where feasible.

AcmeTech Solutions Inc. — Engineering — Internal & Confidential
Page 7

Q: How is schema evolution managed for Kafka events?

A: All event schemas are registered in the Confluent Schema Registry and must maintain
backward compatibility for at least 2 minor versions.

18. Appendix: Request Lifecycle Example
When a customer triggers a workflow via the API, the request first hits the API Gateway,
which validates the bearer token against the Auth Service and applies rate limiting. The

consumes that event to send any configured customer alert, while the Analytics pipeline

AcmeTech maintains three environments: dev (continuous deployment on every merge to

AcmeTech observes a deployment freeze on non-critical changes during the last 3

AcmeTech covers 100% of the employee premium and 70% of dependent premiums for the
AcmeTech Gold PPO health plan, administered by BlueHarbor Health. Two additional plan
tiers (Silver and Bronze) are available with lower Company contribution levels.
Dental and vision coverage are provided at no cost to the employee under the AcmeTech
Complete plan.
2. Retirement Savings
Employees in the United States are eligible to enroll in the 401(k) plan on their first day of
employment. AcmeTech matches 100% of employee contributions up to 4% of base salary,
with immediate vesting.
Employees in Canada, Ireland, India, and Singapore are enrolled in country-specific
retirement programs (RRSP matching, PRSA, PF, and CPF supplements respectively) as
described in the regional benefits addendum.
3. Wellness Stipend
Every employee receives a $75 USD monthly wellness stipend (or local currency
equivalent) that can be used for gym memberships, fitness classes, mental health apps, or
therapy co-pays. The stipend is administered through the Forma platform and does not roll
over month to month.

Birthing parents receive 16 weeks of fully paid leave. Non-birthing parents and adoptive
parents receive 10 weeks of fully paid leave. Leave can be taken continuously or split into
two blocks within the first 12 months after the birth or adoption date.
5. Equity Compensation
Eligible employees receive a stock option grant (Incentive Stock Options or Non-Qualified
Stock Options depending on jurisdiction) that vests over 4 years with a 1-year cliff, at 25%
after year one and monthly thereafter. Refresh grants are considered annually during the
October performance cycle.

Perks include a $1,000 USD annual learning and development stipend, a one-time $500
home office setup allowance for hybrid/remote employees, and a company-wide winter
shutdown between December 24 and January 1 in addition to standard PTO.

themselves and dependents at group rates.

outside of Open Enrollment within 30 days of the event.

This HR Policy Manual governs employment terms and workplace conduct for all
employees of AcmeTech Solutions Inc. ("AcmeTech" or "the Company"), including full-time,
part-time, and contract staff working from any of the Company's six global offices: San
Francisco (HQ), Austin, Toronto, Dublin, Bengaluru, and Singapore.
2. Equal Employment Opportunity
AcmeTech is an equal opportunity employer. Hiring, promotion, compensation, and
termination decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin,
age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, or gender identity.
Any employee who believes they have experienced discrimination should report the matter
to People Operations (people-ops@acmetech.com) or use the anonymous Ethics Hotline at
1-800-555-0199.
3. Working Hours and Attendance
Standard working hours are 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM local time, Monday through Friday, with a
one-hour unpaid lunch break. AcmeTech operates a flexible-hours policy allowing
employees to shift their start time between 7:00 AM and 10:00 AM as long as core
collaboration hours (10:00 AM - 3:00 PM local time) are maintained.

Hybrid employees are required to be in-office a minimum of 2 days per week (Tuesday and
Thursday are designated anchor days). Fully remote roles are approved on a case-by-case
basis by the hiring VP.
4. Probation Period
All new hires undergo a 90-day probationary period. Performance and cultural fit are
reviewed at the 30-day and 90-day marks by the hiring manager in partnership with People
Operations. Probation may be extended by a maximum of 30 additional days at manager
discretion.
5. Performance Reviews
Formal performance reviews are conducted twice annually, in April and October, using the
AcmeTech Growth Framework, which rates employees on a 5-point scale across three
dimensions: Impact, Craft, and Collaboration.
Employees rated 'Exceeds Expectations' or higher for two consecutive cycles are eligible
for accelerated promotion review.
6. Code of Conduct
Employees are expected to act with integrity, respect confidentiality of Company and
customer data, and avoid conflicts of interest. Gifts from vendors or partners valued over
$75 USD must be declined or reported to a manager.
Violations of the Code of Conduct are addressed through a progressive discipline process:
verbal warning, written warning, final written warning, and termination, though the Company

7. Termination and Offboarding
Voluntary resignation requires a minimum of 2 weeks' written notice for individual
contributors and 4 weeks for managers and above. Involuntary termination decisions must
be reviewed and approved by People Operations and Legal prior to communication to the
employee.
All Company property, including laptops, access badges, and security tokens, must be
returned within 5 business days of the employee's last working day.

People Operations - owns policy interpretation, maintains the HR Policy Manual, and
handles escalations.


reviews, and performance management for their direct reports.


arrangements) and review disciplinary escalations.

interim measures (such as temporary schedule or reporting-line changes) available to
protect the complainant during investigation.

1. Paid Time Off (PTO)
Full-time employees accrue 22 days of PTO per year, front-loaded at the start of each
calendar year for employees with more than 1 year of tenure. New hires accrue PTO
monthly during their first year (1.83 days per month).
A maximum of 5 unused PTO days may be carried over into the following calendar year;
any balance above this is forfeited on December 31, except where prohibited by local law.
2. Sick Leave
Employees receive 10 paid sick days per year, separate from PTO. Sick leave may also be
used to care for an immediate family member. No doctor's note is required for absences of
2 days or fewer.
3. Public Holidays
AcmeTech observes 11 public holidays per year based on the employee's local office
calendar, published annually by People Operations by December 1 of the prior year.
4. Bereavement Leave
Employees receive up to 10 paid days of bereavement leave for the death of an immediate
family member and up to 3 paid days for extended family.

AcmeTech Solutions Inc. — HR — Internal & Confidential
Page 4
5. Leave Request Process
All leave requests must be submitted through Workday at least 5 business days in advance
for planned absences. Manager approval is required within 2 business days of submission.
Unplanned sick leave should be reported to the direct manager before the start of the
workday via Slack or phone.
6. Sabbatical Leave
Employees who reach 5 years of continuous tenure are eligible for a 4-week paid
sabbatical, to be scheduled with at least 60 days' notice and manager approval.
7. Jury Duty and Civic Leave
Employees summoned for jury duty receive full pay for up to 10 business days; pay beyond
this period may be supplemented by the employee's remaining PTO balance. Employees
voting in a public election are permitted up to 2 hours of paid leave if their work schedule
does not otherwise allow time to vote.
8. Military Leave
AcmeTech complies with applicable military leave laws (such as USERRA in the United
States), providing job-protected unpaid leave for employees called to active duty, with
continuation of health benefits during the leave period as required by law.

AcmeTech Solutions Inc. — HR — Internal & Confidential
Page 5
9. Extended Medical Leave
Employees with a qualifying serious health condition may take up to 12 weeks of
job-protected leave per year (26 weeks for care of a covered service member), running
concurrently with any applicable short-term disability benefit. Extended medical leave
requests are coordinated through People Operations and, where applicable, the Company's
leave administration partner.
10. Unpaid Personal Leave
Employees with at least 1 year of tenure may request up to 4 weeks of unpaid personal
leave per calendar year for reasons not covered by other leave categories, subject to
manager and People Operations approval and business needs.
11. Leave Balance and Payout
Accrued and unused PTO (up to the carryover cap) is paid out upon voluntary or
involuntary termination in accordance with local law. Sick leave balances are not paid out
upon termination, as sick leave is intended solely to cover active need.
12. Manager Responsibilities
Managers are responsible for reviewing direct reports' leave balances quarterly to
encourage PTO usage, approving or denying leave requests within 2 business days, and
ensuring adequate team coverage is arranged before approving overlapping leave requests
within the same team.

Workflows are built visually using drag-and-drop 'nodes' representing triggers, conditions,
and actions. Each workflow can include up to 50 nodes on the Growth tier and unlimited
nodes on Enterprise.
3. Triggers and Actions
Triggers determine when a workflow runs (e.g., 'New record created in Salesforce,'
'Scheduled - every day at 9 AM'). Actions determine what happens next (e.g., 'Send Slack
message,' 'Update record in NetSuite').
4. Testing and Publishing
Workflows can be run in Test Mode using sample data before publishing live. Once
published, a workflow's execution history and any errors can be reviewed in the Run History
tab, which retains 90 days of logs on the Growth tier and 1 year on Enterprise.

Workflows can be shared with teammates with View, Edit, or Admin permission levels.

Advanced users can use Formulas (a spreadsheet-like expression syntax) within workflow
nodes to transform data, and Sub-Workflows to modularize commonly reused automation
logic across multiple parent workflows.

Each workflow node can be configured with custom error-handling behavior: Retry (default,
up to 3 attempts), Skip and Continue, or Halt Workflow. Critical nodes (e.g., payment
processing steps) should generally be configured to Halt Workflow on error to prevent
partial execution.

8. Network Security
Production infrastructure is segmented into public, private, and data subnets with security
groups enforcing least-privilege network access between tiers. All internal
service-to-service traffic is encrypted using mutual TLS (mTLS).
9. Endpoint Security
All Company laptops run CrowdStrike endpoint detection and response (EDR) software,
with alerts routed to the IT Security team's 24/7 monitoring queue. Employees may not
disable or uninstall EDR software; attempts to do so trigger an automatic alert.
10. Physical Security
All AcmeTech offices require badge access, with visitor sign-in and escort required for
anyone without a Company badge. Server rooms and network closets are restricted to
authorized IT Security and Facilities personnel only.
11. Secure Software Development Lifecycle
Security requirements are integrated into the software development lifecycle via mandatory
static analysis (SAST) and dependency scanning in CI, and an annual penetration test
conducted by an independent third-party firm covering the production environment.

12. Security Awareness Training
All employees complete mandatory security awareness training within their first 2 weeks of
employment and annually thereafter, covering phishing recognition, password hygiene, and
data handling. Simulated phishing exercises are run quarterly, with repeat-click employees
required to complete supplemental training.
13. Bring Your Own Device (BYOD)
Personal devices may access Company email and calendar through a managed mobile
profile enforcing a device passcode and remote wipe capability, but may not be used to
access source code repositories, production systems, or Restricted-tier data.
